approachQuestion.prompt: Find the minimum number of edges between two vertices in an unweighted undirected graph.

options.text: Run breadth-first search from the start and record each first distance.
options.feedback: BFS discovers vertices in increasing distance layers.

options.text: Run Dijkstra with a minimum heap and unit edge weights.
options.feedback: The result is right, but the heap is unnecessary for equal edge weights.

options.text: Run breadth-first search from the finish and read the start distance.
options.feedback: Undirected edges make the distance symmetric.

options.text: Return the first path found by depth-first search.
options.feedback: The first path found need not be the shortest.

feedback.reason: Unweighted equal-cost edges make graph traversal order decisive.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Choose the time and additional-space pair for BFS from the start.
constraints: V is the vertex count; E is the edge count.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) additional space
O((V + E) log V) time, O(V) additional space

feedback.reason: Each vertex is queued once and each adjacency is examined a bounded number of times.

methodReveal.title: Breadth-first layers
methodReveal.description: Use a queue and mark a vertex with its distance when first discovered; the queue then processes complete distance layers.
